decisions.reason: As an adjacent dietary-supplement range with several variants, it is a relatively low-cost option that still supports portfolio broadening and is worth keeping open.
This skin and hair supplement sits close to the consumer-health portfolio and is inexpensive to carry, so we would keep it despite a likely crowded market.
Joint-health supplements fit the pharmacy channel and an aging customer base, so the product still has enough option value to remain on the market.
The immune supplement is more trend-sensitive and uncertain than the other supplements, but its low carrying cost and fit with the existing Trivital line justify keeping it for now.
A more distant generic with an early quality-related problem puts trust and compliance resources at risk, so its downside now appears to outweigh its remaining option value.

This more distant OTC migraine product likely requires continued commercial support, and with limited evidence of traction we would reallocate resources to stronger adjacent products and development projects.
